intended_object: The `w`-IPC property of a category C that has `w`-small products and `w`-small filtered colimits (Kashiwara–Schapira, Def. 3.1.10). For every `w`-small index set A, every family of `w`-small filtered categories I_a and every family of functors F_a : I_a → C, the canonical map colim_{(i_a) ∈ ∏ I_a} ∏_a F_a(i_a) → ∏_a colim F_a is an isomorphism. The source is the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`IsIPC` asks C to have `w`-small products and `w`-small filtered colimits, exactly as Kashiwara–Schapira assume. It then requires `IsIPCOfShape.{w} ι C` for every `ι : Type w`.

`IsIPCOfShape` says the following. Take any family of small filtered categories `J i : Type w` with functors `F i : J i ⥤ C`, and take colimit cocones `c i` on the `F i`. Then the cocone `coconePointwiseProduct c` on `pointwiseProduct F` is a colimit cocone. That cocone has point `∏ᶜ (c i).pt` and is built on the diagram `(k_i) ↦ ∏ F_i(k_i)` over the product category `Π i, J i`. This is equivalent to the canonical map colim ∏ → ∏ colim being an isomorphism (`IsIPCOfShape.of_isIso` and the `IsIso` instance show this). So it is exactly the IPC condition for index sets of shape ι.

Quantifying over all `ι : Type w` gives all `w`-small index sets. The library also transfers the property to any `Small.{w}` index type along `equivShrink`.

The assumption `HasFilteredColimitsOfSize` is not used in the body. It only limits the class to categories that have filtered colimits, as the textbook definition does. Universe-polymorphic smallness is the natural generality here. Mathlib has no other definition of this notion.
